name: The Langham, London
insider_take: Europe's first "grand hotel" still reigns supreme on Regent Street, where literary legends once penned masterpieces and afternoon tea was elevated to an art form.
whats_special: The Langham holds the prestigious title of being Europe's first luxury hotel, opening in 1865. Famous guests include Oscar Wilde, Mark Twain, and Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, who actually set several Sherlock Holmes stories here. The hotel's Palm Court is credited with creating the tradition of afternoon tea with live classical music.
pro_tip: Book the Sterling Suite where Sir Arthur Conan Doyle stayed while writing his Sherlock Holmes stories - you'll find original Victorian details and literary memorabilia throughout.
dont_miss: The legendary afternoon tea at Palm Court (consistently rated among the world's best), and a visit to the hotel's secret BBC connection - Broadcasting House is directly across the street, and many BBC personalities have called The Langham their London home-away-from-home for decades.
pros: Historic luxury hotel with elegant Victorian architecture and timeless sophistication
Prime location on Regent Street with easy access to Oxford Circus and West End theaters
World-renowned Artesian bar and exceptional fine dining restaurants
Luxurious Chuan Body + Soul spa offering traditional Chinese wellness treatments
cons: Premium pricing reflects luxury positioning and central London location
Historic building may have smaller room sizes compared to modern hotels
